performance.cost_breakdown: catalog parts $563, filament 2.07 kg $52, fasteners $14, fabricated/other $61 (Ø 236 x 3 mm aluminium disc deck, laser cut (~$30); 20 x 2 mm aluminium tube, 0.45 m (~$8); two 8-LED WS2812 sticks behind translucent eye diffusers (~$8); power switch, 15 A fuse, wiring)

assumptions: EVA cannot hover: this EVA rolls on a hidden differential-drive base (two 37D gearmotors, two ball casters) under a dark skirt; the egg rides on a 20 mm aluminium spine above it, so the gap reads as the film's hover.

The egg body is four printed PETG shell segments (two bands, two halves) screwed to two printed ribs on the spine; the head is one print (230 x 200 x 150 mm) with a dark visor band and two LED eye diffusers.
The head turns on a single pan servo; the film's free-floating head tilt is not reproduced. The arms are two-servo fins hanging beside the egg (they cannot fold flush into the body like the film's).
The camera looks out through a 12 mm hole in the visor centre.
